title: Import watermarks need committed side-effect evidence
summary: An import watermark or success marker should advance only from committed side effects. Audit rows and progress evidence must not become resume truth until the durable write they describe has actually succeeded.
ai_value: Helps agents distinguish in-flight progress, audit visibility, committed watermarks, and external acknowledgements when repairing imports or retries.

contexts: incremental imports maintain watermarks, cursors, audit rows, or progress tables
a partial run wrote evidence rows but failed during the downstream side effect
uniform downstream exceptions make agents suspect the upstream provider first

trigger_signals.description: A watermark advances before the destination mutation commits.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Treat the watermark as unsafe; separate in-flight cursor from committed lower bound.

trigger_signals.description: Evidence rows are written before the side effect they claim to prove.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Make those rows attempt/audit state only, not resume state.

trigger_signals.description: A whole batch fails with the same downstream exception class after source reads succeed.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Investigate the local side-effect path before assuming an upstream outage.

negative_signals.description: The destination operation is atomic with the watermark update in one durable transaction.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: The completion boundary may already be correct, though external acknowledgements still need review.

negative_signals.description: The progress evidence is explicitly labelled attempt-only and never read by resume logic.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Attempt logs can be useful without becoming committed state.

common_wrong_assumptions: If source reads succeeded, the import can advance the watermark.
Audit rows are harmless even when resume logic later reads them as truth.
A uniform exception across the batch must mean the upstream system is down.

first_checks.check: Trace the order of source read, destination write, audit/progress write, watermark advance, and external acknowledgement.
first_checks.why: The committed side effect must be the boundary for success.

first_checks.check: Probe a failed run and verify whether its rows can influence future resume lower bounds.
first_checks.why: Failed attempts should be visible but not promoted automatically.
Uniform local exceptions usually require code/config repair, not upstream backoff.

decision_rules.condition: A watermark, lower bound, or success marker advances before durable destination commit.
decision_rules.then: Move the state transition after the committed side effect and keep in-flight cursors separate.

decision_rules.condition: Failed attempt evidence exists but is not safe for resume.
decision_rules.then: Keep it visible for audit while excluding it from resume selection unless a reviewed repair promotes it.

decision_rules.condition: Uniform downstream exceptions appear after successful source reads.
decision_rules.then: Inspect local destination schema, permissions, serialization, and transaction boundaries before broad upstream retries.

do_not: Do not let failed-run cursors become committed watermarks by accident.
Do not acknowledge external notifications before the local persistence contract is satisfied; see webhook-ack-layer-and-auth-identity.
Do not hide partial attempts; make them audit-visible but not authoritative.
Do not use committed side-effect evidence as a substitute for persisted cursor-key design; cross-check progress-state-must-match-cursor-semantics when modes/windows can overwrite progress state.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: Trace the import state transitions and ensure only committed destination effects can advance resume or watermark truth.

risk.notes: This record is de-identified agent guidance. It does not authorize bypassing maintainer, security, publication, production, billing, data, permission, or destructive-action gates.
